title: Hytale runtime common assets sent with setup-only progress after world join
summary: Atmosphere Tool 1.3.1 streamed generated fog assets through sendAssetsToPlayer, causing a WorldLoadProgress packet after Playing and a client disconnect. Version 1.3.2 omits the setup-only progress packet; the affected world reached InGame with no disconnect. Client parsing of generated blockyanim files remains a separate open failure.
problem_class: protocol packet valid only during connection setup sent during active play
problem_description: Joining an existing Zytale singleplayer world disconnects after entering Playing because WorldLoadProgress arrives late.
context: A large enabled fog area near the player is generated by Atmosphere Tool 1.3.1 after world join. The renderer invokes CommonAssetModule.sendAssetsToPlayer while the client is Playing; this built-in method inserts WorldLoadProgress between AssetInitialize and AssetPart. A prior successful log used Atmosphere Tool 1.3.0.
capabilities_required: dynamic common asset transfer to one player
constraints: preserve existing fog area data and stable plugin identity
client test needed before declaring resolved
known_attempts: AdaptiveWindow 0.4.3 removed invalid item texture warnings but the disconnect persisted

solution_versions.description: Atmosphere Tool 1.3.2 replaces the setup-oriented sendAssetsToPlayer call with targeted runtime asset packets: AssetInitialize, AssetPart, AssetFinalize, then RequestCommonAssetsRebuild. It preserves generated fog models and area data without sending WorldLoadProgress after the client enters Playing.
changes: Introduce RuntimeAssetSender to prepare ordered asset transfer packets without WorldLoadProgress
Use the runtime sender from FogVolumeRenderer for each playing client
Keep native 2,621,440-byte asset chunks and final rebuild request
Bump manifest and packaged JAR to 1.3.2 while keeping plugin identity stable
advantages: Removes the exact setup-only packet that the Hytale client rejects during active play
Targets only the player missing the generated assets
Preserves existing fog geometry, item IDs and saved area data
disadvantages: A real client reconnect to the affected world is still required to verify the disconnection is gone
Runtime sender mirrors the current Hytale 0.7.0 asset packet sequence and must be rechecked after protocol changes
test_results: Java 25 build and packaged JAR validation passed on Hytale 0.7.0
Packet regression verifies large multipart payload, asset ordering, rebuild, and absence of WorldLoadProgress
Isolated Hytale 0.7.0 server boot and render/replication probe passed
Version 1.3.2 installed in shared Mods with verified backup of 1.3.1; live client test pending

metrics.reliability: Server and packet sequence tests passed; client rejoin pending
metrics.compatibility: Hytale 0.7.0; existing saved fog areas and plugin ID unchanged

solution_versions.description: Atmosphere Tool 1.3.2 replaces the setup-oriented sendAssetsToPlayer call with targeted runtime asset packets. The affected Hytale client entered the world without the prior WorldLoadProgress disconnect; generated fog animations still produced client parsing warnings recorded separately.
changes: Send AssetInitialize, AssetPart and AssetFinalize directly during Playing
Request common-asset rebuild after the complete transfer
Keep the stable plugin identity and saved fog-area data unchanged
advantages: Eliminates the observed setup-stage packet violation
Allows the affected world to reach InGame
disadvantages: Generated blocky animations emit client NullReferenceException and parse warnings
test_results: Affected-world client log 2026-10-13_19-34-10 loaded Atmosphere Tool 1.3.2
GameInstance.OnWorldJoined and transition to InGame recorded once
Zero WorldLoadProgress-at-Playing errors and zero disconnects recorded
Thirty parsing warnings affected nineteen distinct generated blockyanim assets

metrics.reliability: WorldLoadProgress disconnect resolved in one affected-world client run
metrics.compatibility: Hytale 0.7.0; animation parsing remains an open limitation

transferability: Other Hytale mods that stream generated CommonAsset files during Playing must avoid sendAssetsToPlayer because it emits a setup-only progress packet in Hytale 0.7.0; revalidate on future versions.
